Nadia (AM): Heads-up: Citrine Labs wants to convert their POC -> enterprise commit. Key asks: reserved GPUs for predictable cost/latency, autoscale for product launches, hard burst-spend cap, and answers on KMS + audit retention. They mix chat + nightly embedding batches.

Omar (SE): Short traffic profile they sent: steady 80 qps daytime, nightly embedding jobs ~200 concurrent jobs, occasional campaign bursts to ~1.6k qps for 90-180s. Avg tokens: chat 120 in / 100 out, embeddings jobs vary 2048 tokens. p95 target 250ms, p99 500ms.

Priya (SRE): Sizing quick-math from our perf runs (decoder-only int8): conservative steady-state per GPU ~40 qps at p95=250ms for ~220 token sequences without batching. With KV caching and modest batching you can reach ~70 qps. For baseline 80 qps reserve 2 GPUs (conservative) or 1 if they accept tight headroom. Recommend 3 GPUs if they want a 2x safety margin and embedding job isolation.

Omar (SE): Burst delta = 1600 - 80 = 1520 qps. If we rely on same model @40 qps/GPU -> ~38 GPUs. But propose hybrid: reserved pool (3 GPUs) + burst runway using: (a) quantized "burst" replica (~100 qps/GPU), (b) aggressive batching during spikes, (c) routing embeddings to a separate reserved pool at night. With burst model at 100 qps/GPU -> ~15 GPUs needed.

Priya (SRE): Operational playbook highlights:
- KV/cache warm: schedule a warm job 10 minutes before expected blasts.
- Synthetic warm command we use in staging:

  ./warm_tool --qps 1200 --concurrency 240 --seq 220 --duration 120

- Eviction strategy: cross-AZ spread + spot fallback.
- Degradation ladder when burst cap hit: full model -> quantized model -> shorten responses -> deny non-critical embedding jobs.

Luca (Sales Eng): Pricing options to propose:
1) Committed: 3 reserved GPUs + monthly platform fee + 12mo discount.
2) Committed + burst credits: pre-purchase X GPU-minutes/month at a discounted burst rate, with tenant hard-cap option.
3) BYO private license: adds one-time licensing + integration.

Nadia (AM): They explicitly asked for a hard spend cap with automatic fallback. Priya, can we implement a tenant-level hard cap and automated degradation flow?

Priya (SRE): Yes. We can implement hard cap + alerting + auto-fallback to quantized model or regional spill. We'll document expected SLOs per fallback step.

Omar (SE): I'll produce a 1-page capacity calc (assumptions + GPU counts) and a simple cost table showing committed vs burst vs pay-as-you-go. Luca will draft contract language for burst credits + hard cap. Priya will add the runbook + KMS/audit steps.

ticket-bot: Created POC-8712 "Citrine Labs commit: reserved pool + burst-runway + hard-cap" assigned to @Omar @Priya @Luca.

Nadia (AM): Meeting in 1 hour to finalize slides. Short sync after runbook is drafted. Thanks.
